title: Sprite2D with shader containing `uniform float` parameter causes greyed out texture to flash over the screen for 1 frame
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducable in: 4.4-stable, 4.4.1-stable, 4.5-dev5 (tested 2025-06-13)

### System information

Godot v4.4.stable.mono - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated GeForce MX250 - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10510U CPU @ 1.80GHz (8 threads)

### Issue description

After I added a pulsating shader to one of my sprites (Sprite2D), I noticed that the screen flashed briefly every time I entered the particular scene that the sprite belonged to. After some investigation, it looks like the flashing image is a greyed out and streched out version of the sprite texture appearing for around 1 frame. After that flash everything seems to work as normal, inclluding the shader doing what it should.

After some more investigation I pinpointed the problem to the `uniform float pulse_speed` parameter for the shader.

- If I removed that and just used a hardcoded value instead, the problem disappeared.
- If I commented out the rest of the shader code and just left the `uniform float pulse_speed` parameter, the problem was still there.

Some other findings:

- If I remove the shader completely, the problem disappears.
- If I make the sprite invisible (`Visible = false`), the problem disappears.
- If I start the scene with the sprite invisible, and then turn it visible again after say a 1.5 second delay (`Visible = true` or `Show()`), then the flashing texture problem also appears after that 1.5 second delay.
- If I try and make the sprite visible again slowly using a tween and "modulate", the flashing texture appears as soon as the sprite is no longer 100 % transparent (i.e. when the tween starts). This seems to happen even If I start the tween after a delay.
- The problem is NOT present with the Compatibility renderer selected, but it happens for the Forward+ and Mobile renderers.

It feels to me that whatever-the-problem-is has something to do with when the sprite/shader is rendered to the screen for the first time. I have not been able to test this on another computer, so maybe it's something very specific to my laptop, I don't know...

#### The shader code
```
shader_type canvas_item;

uniform float pulse_speed = 3.f; // commenting this out makes the problem disappear

void fragment() {
	// Called for every pixel the material is visible on.
	//float pulse_speed = 3.f;
	float t = 0.5f + 0.5f * sin(TIME * pulse_speed); // between [0.0, 1.0]
	float addend = t * 0.2f - 0.1f; // between [-0.1, 0.1]
	COLOR.r = clamp(COLOR.r + addend, 0.f, 1.f);
	COLOR.g = clamp(COLOR.g + addend, 0.f, 1.f);
	COLOR.b = clamp(COLOR.b + addend, 0.f, 1.f);
}
```

#### Video and screenshot
Youtube video showing the problem: https://youtu.be/suCwwgpLMfc?si=u6H8BaurOuk3m9nT

Screenshot of the frame where the glitch happens.
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1887612b-33a1-4996-9979-91c1ab2d2649)

### Steps to reproduce

When running the MRP, you should see a button "Start". Clicking that button changes scene to the "game scene", where the sprite and its shader is. Directly when the game scene is loaded, there should be one frame of a glitchy greyed out big texture.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Github link: https://github.com/Plankton555/sprite_shader_bug_repro

The zip contains both the C# project and a converted gdscript version of it. The problem appears in both.
[sprite_shader_bug_repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20720176/sprite_shader_bug_repro.zip)
